newsitem.title: MONACO: SOCCER SHOWCASE-HENRY HELPS MONACO REACH NEW HEIGHTS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-HENRY HELPS MONACO REACH NEW HEIGHTS.

text.p: Teenager Thierry Henry is a symbol of the new strength of runaway French league leaders Monaco, who should rely on him again when they meet Marseille on Saturday.
Ironically, 19-year-old striker Henry is often a substitute and will probably leave the club at the end of the season.
But nevertheless, he has undoubtably been a key factor in Monaco's formidable season.

He has played few full matches in the first division but his second-half appearances in the French league have been enough for him to score eight goals and he has netted a further four in the UEFA Cup.
In the absence of Nigerian striker Viktor Ikpeba, called up for international duties, Henry should start the match against Marseille at stade Louis II.
Even more than Arsenal's Patrick Vieira and Nicolas Anelka, Henry is regarded by many as the most promising player of France's talented new generation.
He is also likely to illustrate new practices typical of the era opened by the Bosman ruling as he is said to be on his way to Real Madrid.

The bad example set by Vieira, who wasted an entire season on AC Milan's bench before joining Arsenal, will apparently not stop Henry from moving to the Spanish club, who claim to have a document signed by him.

"I'm aware everything could stop at once," said Henry, who nevertheless dreams of walking in the footsteps of Didier Deschamps and Zinedine Zidane, both key-players for Europe's finest club side Juventus.

Other players like Marcel Desailly at AC Milan, Eric Cantona at Manchester United and David Ginola at Newcastle will probably have also influenced Henry's future by making French players the most sought after in Europe.
"Everybody tells me to be careful and I will be," Henry promised.
Monaco took a chance on him two years ago after hearing he had scored six goals in a fourth division match.
The interest in the under-21 international, brought up in the Parisian working class suburb of Les Ullis, has never stopped growing since.

Tall and fast, Henry had been spotted by several athletics clubs as a potential sprint champion. But he chose football and soon worked miracles with his physical strength, fine technique and genuine scoring instinct.
"I had never imagined that things could go that fast," he said. "Only two years ago I was playing with the under 17s. I thought I would have to learn my trade with Monaco's reserves."
Henry should soon make it to the top as national team boss Aime Jacquet has already expressed interest in him.
Jacquet called France's latest prodigy in a group of 37 players selected for tests ahead of a friendly with Sweden won 1-0 by the home side at Parc des Princes earlier this month.

"He has Patrick Vieira's experience to help him", said France's under-21 manager Raymond Domenech. "I'm sure he can work from that. It is intelligence, not talent, that brings a player to the very best level."
